result.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
result.summary: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input. We find that the shared component suffices for most of the adaptation gain and can be learned directly: a shift adapter that learns a constant vector per layer, identical for every input, reproduces the behavior of LoRA and full fine-tuning. We call this the potentiality principle of foundation models: the base model already contains the capacity needed for task-specific expertise. To adapt to a new task, the model just needs to be actualized, i.e., pushed in a certain direction via a constant, input-independent shift. We show the implications of this principle on parameter-efficient adaptation, steering, and convergence across models, and how it explains the neural thickets phenomenon.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 LoRA 与全参数微调等适配引起的更新分解为「所有输入共享的常数分量」与「随输入变化的残差」，发现共享分量已能解释大部分适配增益，且用每层一个与输入无关的常数向量（shift adapter）即可复现原适配行为，据此提出基础模型的「潜在性—现实性」原则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「输入无关常数偏移 vs 输入相关残差」的分解思路可供核查：latent/推理状态的训练增益究竟是整层漂移还是样例特异计算，可能为 LVR 的贡献分配与监督设计提供分析工具。
